description:
pkix-profiles/src/lib.rs lines 161-179: WebPkiProfile::policy(now_unix) sets p.max_validity_secs = Some(sc081_validity_cap(now_unix)), where now_unix is the current wall-clock time. But pkix-path chain_walk checks max_validity_secs against (notAfter - notBefore) for every cert in the chain (not as a lookup against notBefore). The SC-081 text says "the cap in effect at issuance time governs the cert for its lifetime." A cert issued before 2026-03-15 under the 398-day cap is permanently subject to the 398-day cap regardless of when the relying party validates it.

With WebPkiProfile.policy(now_unix) at a 2026-06-01 relying party time: sc081_validity_cap(now_unix) = 200 days. A cert validly issued with 365-day validity on 2026-01-01 (under the 398-day cap then in force) would fail max_validity_secs = 200 days, even though it was compliant at issuance. This is a false rejection.

The ValidityMaxLint in pkix-lint correctly evaluates the cap at notBefore (cabf_tls_br.rs line 121). The profile-level enforcement in pkix-profiles does not match this correct interpretation.

Correct fix: do not set max_validity_secs in WebPkiProfile — rely on ValidityMaxLint for this check. Or, if max_validity_secs must be set in the profile, it should be set to the issuance-time cap (which requires knowing notBefore, not just now_unix). The profile policy() approach is structurally incapable of expressing "apply the cap as of notBefore" because max_validity_secs is a single u64 applied uniformly.

Note: the test at pkix-profiles/src/lib.rs line 675 explicitly narrows the cap to 300 days and expects rejection of a 365-day cert — this test documents the behavior but the behavior is incorrect per SC-081 semantics.
title: P0: WebPkiProfile applies SC-081 cap at validation time (now_unix), not at cert issuance time
